title: More than one agent
about: Every file in this film is read from this repository as it stands, and every line of terminal output is replayed from docs/manual/captures, recorded by running plain shell commands for real; nothing in it is a command of Orthograph's.

scenes.title: One owner for each line of work

lines.text: Until now, one agent worked on Plugged In at a time. The next stage is bigger. You want several building at once.
Two agents in the same files undo each other's work, and neither notices.
Orthograph has no command for this yet. So this film leaves Plugged In, and shows how this repository builds Orthograph itself.
Every line of work has one owner, called a goal: one long-running agent that manages others. We asked the map which goals run.
Three. One builds the framework. One builds an app on it. One builds nothing new: it brings finished work into the shared branch.
Before a goal builds anything, it claims it.
The status page keeps one row for each piece of work. A claim is two cells of that row: the lane, which names the goal, and the paths it will change.
Here, goal sixteen holds this piece, and names two folders. Any other agent that needs those folders reads this first.
We counted the claims held today. Thirteen for the app's goal. One for the framework's. Every other lane says none.
An agent building an app keeps finding gaps in the framework under it. Whose are they? One rule, three cases.
Case one. A running goal already has it. Wait, or take the part that has landed.
Case two. It would change paths another goal has claimed. One named goal settles it: one of them does it, or they split it.
Case three. Neither. Claim it, and build it.
Only the second case needs a decision.

scenes.title: A list that may only shrink

lines.text: Checks are written before the build, by a different agent. So red checks sit in the shared branch before the code that passes them.
To keep that branch a gate, each failure we know about is written in a list. The build fails on any failure that is not listed.
Here is one whole list, about Plugged In's own journeys. One line says why the entry is there. The other names the one check that may fail.
A builder may delete a line, and may never add one. A script in this repository's CI refuses the pull request.
lines.say: A builder may delete a line, and may never add one. A script in this repository's C I refuses the pull request.

lines.text: Ten lists today. The smallest holds one file. Over time, the numbers go down.
What goes wrong. A claim is a cell in a table. Nothing locks the paths, so two agents can still meet in one file, as a merge conflict.
And a claim can go stale, when a goal stops and leaves its lane set.
One honest note. Everything you watched is this repository's practice. No ortho command claims work, settles a collision, or keeps a list.
Nothing here was run on Plugged In. We read files, and counted them with plain shell.
The product's answer is called the factory: a board that agents build from. It is designed, and not built.
This is the manual's closing chapter, so nothing comes next. What you can copy today is small: one file of claims, one rule, and one list that only shrinks.

pictures.owners: You, then the goals: a terminal replays captures/agents-goals.txt, and its three lines become three lanes across the sheet, the picture every later sheet returns to.
pictures.claim: The builder's goal acting: an editor quotes line 224 of docs/canon/status.md with the lane cell and the Touches cell lit, the two folders drop into lane sixteen as a claim, and a terminal replays captures/agents-claims.txt for the counts.
pictures.rule: An editor quotes lines 29 to 36 of design/goals/map.md, one case lit at a time, and each case is played on the three lanes: a piece waits, two lanes reach for one path and Goal 18 settles it, a free piece is claimed.
pictures.ratchet: The author, then the builder: an editor quotes both lines of e2e/stage1/expected-failing/01-plugged-in-journeys.txt, a line is shown leaving and an added line refused, and a terminal replays captures/agents-ratchets.txt, its ten counts drawn as bars computed from the recording.
pictures.standing: The three lanes once more with Kit.stand over them: claims, the collision rule and the ratchet marked practice, the factory marked missing (the work-factory row of docs/canon/status.md, quoted), and no terminal that is not a replay.
pictures.carries: The lanes: one lane for each running goal, read from captures/agents-goals.txt, with claimed paths sitting in them; it opens the film, takes the claim, plays the three cases, and closes under the standing marks.
